entities.name: CAG
entities.line: Art 148 | appointed by President | 6 yrs/65 | removed like SC judge | audit reports → President/Governor (Art 151)
facts: Art 148–151; oath under 3rd Schedule
Salary = SC judge; charged on Consolidated Fund of India
Audits Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund & Public Account of Union + States
Union audit reports → President → laid in Parliament → examined by PAC
Called 'friend, philosopher & guide' of PAC
traps: After tenure, NOT eligible for any further office under GoI/States (Art 148(4))
Only auditor — no 'control' over release of funds (unlike UK Comptroller)
Not an officer or member of Parliament (unlike UK C&AG) but acts as Parliament's agent in audit; removal only like SC judge (Art 148(1))
6-yr/65 tenure & duties fixed by CAG (DPC) Act 1971, NOT by the Constitution; resigns to President

entities.name: Election Commission of India
entities.line: Art 324 | CEC + ECs appointed by President on rec. of Selection Committee: PM + LoP (LS) + Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM (CEC & Other ECs Act 2023) | 6 yrs/65 | CEC removed like SC judge; ECs only on CEC's recommendation
facts: Part XV, Art 324–329; Art 324 = superintendence of polls to Parliament, State Legislatures, President, VP
Multi-member since 1993 (briefly 1989); CEC + 2 ECs now; decisions by majority
2023 Act: Search Committee shortlists → Selection Committee (PM + LoP + Union Cabinet Minister)
Anoop Baranwal (2023): SC had put CJI on panel till Parliament legislates → 2023 Act replaced CJI
EC elevated to CEC: total term still max 6 yrs
Panchayat & municipal polls = State Election Commission (Art 243K / 243ZA)
traps: CEC/ECs NOT eligible for re-appointment (2023 Act)
Constitution itself fixes no qualifications or term — left to Parliament
Constitution does not bar retired ECs from later govt posts
ECI does NOT conduct panchayat/municipal elections
Number of ECs = as President fixes (Art 324(2)); Constitution fixes no number
2023 Act: CEC/EC must be or have been Secretary-rank to GoI; an EC elevated to CEC → total term ≤6 yrs

entities.name: UPSC
entities.line: Art 315–323 | Chair + members appointed by President | 6 yrs/65 | removal by President; misbehaviour only after SC inquiry (Art 317)
facts: Number of members: decided by President (not fixed in Constitution)
As nearly as may be ½ of members: ≥10 yrs in office under GoI/State govt (Art 316(1) proviso)
Annual report to President (Art 323); govt explains non-acceptance to Parliament
Advisory body — recommendations not binding
traps: Chairman: NOT eligible for further employment under GoI/States (Art 319)
A member CAN become Chairman of UPSC or an SPSC
Not consulted on reservation for backward classes (Art 16(4))
SPSC members appointed by Governor but removable ONLY by President
Chair/member NOT eligible for re-appointment to the same office (Art 316(3)); a member CAN become UPSC/SPSC Chair (Art 319)

entities.name: Finance Commission
entities.line: Art 280 | constituted by President every 5 yrs | Chair + 4 members | tax devolution + grants-in-aid | 16th FC (Chair: Arvind Panagariya) → award period 2026–31
facts: Qualifications set by FC (Misc. Provisions) Act 1951
1st FC 1951: K.C. Neogy; 15th FC: N.K. Singh (41% devolution)
Vertical (Centre→States) + horizontal (among States) devolution of net tax proceeds
Grants-in-aid: Art 275
traps: Recommendations are advisory, not binding
Art 280 = Finance Commission; Art 282 = discretionary grants (different!)
State Finance Commission for local bodies = Art 243I / 243Y
FC members ARE eligible for re-appointment (FC Misc. Provisions Act 1951) — contrast CAG, UPSC, ECI

entities.name: GST Council
entities.line: Art 279A (101st CAA 2016) | Chair: Union FM | members: MoS Finance + State FMs | decisions by ¾ weighted vote (Centre ⅓, States ⅔)
facts: GST launched 1 Jul 2017
Quorum: ½ of members; Centre ⅓ weight, States ⅔; decisions need ¾ weighted vote
GST 2.0 (eff. 22 Sep 2025): main slabs 5% & 18% + 40% on demerit/sin goods
Art 246A: concurrent power to levy GST; Art 269A: IGST on inter-state supply
traps: Mohit Minerals (2022): Council's recommendations are persuasive, not binding
Alcohol for human consumption is OUTSIDE GST
Petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas, crude: inside GST law but rate not yet notified
Vice-Chair chosen by State members from among themselves (Art 279A(3))
'State' for GST includes UTs with legislature (Art 366(26B)) → Delhi, Puducherry, J&K

entities.name: Attorney General
entities.line: Art 76 | appointed by President | qualified to be SC judge | holds office during President's pleasure; no fixed tenure | may speak in Parliament, no vote (Art 88)
facts: Highest law officer of GoI; right of audience in all courts
Not a full-time govt servant — may take private practice (not against GoI)
Privileges of an MP (Art 105)
traps: NOT a member of the Cabinet
Tenure & removal grounds NOT fixed by Constitution
Solicitor General is not a constitutional post
Remuneration fixed by President (Art 76(4)); State counterpart = Advocate General (Art 165)

entities.name: Supreme Court
entities.line: Art 124 | sanctioned strength 38 = CJI + 37 (SC (No. of Judges) Amdt Act 2026; earlier 34) | appointed by President (collegium) | retire at 65 | removal: special majority each House (Art 124(4)); Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968
facts: Inaugurated 28 Jan 1950 (successor of Federal Court, 1937)
Original (Art 131), writ (Art 32), appellate (132–134), advisory (Art 143)
Court of record (Art 129); review (Art 137); law binding on all courts (Art 141); 'complete justice' (Art 142)
Seat Delhi; elsewhere by CJI with President's approval (Art 130)
traps: Art 32 is itself a Fundamental Right; HC writ power (Art 226) is wider (also legal rights)
Advisory opinion (Art 143) NOT binding on President
No SC/HC judge ever removed — V. Ramaswami motion failed in LS (1993); Soumitra Sen resigned (2011); Yashwant Varma resigned (Apr 2026) mid-process
SC strength is raised by ordinary law under Art 124(1), NOT a Constitutional Amendment (1950: CJI + 7)
Constitution says 'impeachment' only for the President (Art 61); judges are 'removed' (Art 124(4))

entities.name: High Courts
entities.line: Art 214 | judges appointed by President (Art 217) | retire at 62 | removed like SC judge | writ jurisdiction Art 226 (wider than Art 32)
facts: 25 High Courts; oldest: Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1862)
Superintendence over subordinate courts (Art 227)
Common HC for 2+ States/UTs (Art 231) — e.g. Guwahati: Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal
Transfer of judges: President after consulting CJI
traps: HC judges retire at 62 (SC at 65)
Retired HC judge can't practise in the same HC — can in SC/other HCs (Art 220)
Number of HC judges fixed by the President (Art 216), not by Constitution/Parliament; age dispute decided by President after consulting CJI (Art 217(3))

entities.name: NCSC
entities.line: Art 338 | Chair + VC + 3 members appointed by President | reports to President
facts: Multi-member constitutional body since 65th CAA 1990 (earlier a Special Officer)
traps: NCSC also covers the Anglo-Indian community (Art 338(10)); civil-court powers while investigating (Art 338(8))

entities.name: NCST
entities.line: Art 338A (89th CAA 2003) | separated from NCSC in 2004 | appointed by President
traps: Union & every State must consult NCST on major policy affecting STs (Art 338A(9))

entities.name: NCBC
entities.line: Art 338B (102nd CAA 2018) | constitutional status; earlier statutory (NCBC Act 1993) | appointed by President
facts: 105th CAA 2021 restored States' power to identify SEBCs (after Maratha quota ruling)
traps: National Commission for Minorities (1992) & NCW (1990 Act) are statutory, not constitutional
102nd CAA also inserted Art 342A (SEBC lists); NCBC Act 1993 repealed 2018; after 105th CAA States keep their own SEBC lists

entities.name: Inter-State Council
entities.line: Art 263 | set up 1990 on Sarkaria Commission rec. | Chair: PM | members: CMs of states & UTs with legislatures, Administrators of other UTs, 6 Union Cabinet Ministers | recommendatory body
facts: Sarkaria Commission 1983–88; Punchhi Commission 2007–10
Standing Committee chaired by Union Home Minister
traps: Art 263 is permissive — President 'may' establish it
ISC is not a court: it inquires & advises (Art 263); legal Centre–State disputes go to SC (Art 131); Zonal Councils are statutory (SRA 1956)

entities.name: Delimitation
entities.line: Art 82 (LS) / Art 170 (assemblies) | Delimitation Commission orders have force of law; Art 329(a) bars routine challenge, but SC (Kishorchandra Chhanganlal Rathod, 2024) allows review if manifestly arbitrary | LS seat allocation frozen on 1971 census till first census after 2026 (84th CAA 2001)
facts: Delimitation Commissions: 1952, 1963, 1973, 2002 (four)
2002 Commission: Justice Kuldip Singh; J&K panel (2020): Justice Ranjana Desai
traps: Orders laid before LS/Assemblies but cannot be modified by them
87th CAA 2003: constituency boundaries readjusted on 2001 census; inter-State SEAT ALLOCATION still on 1971 census

entities.name: Governor
entities.line: Art 153–162 | appointed by President (Art 155) | 5 yrs, holds office during President's pleasure (Art 156) | assent to bills Art 200; reserve for President Art 201
facts: Qualification: citizen, 35 yrs
Same person can be Governor of 2+ States (7th CAA 1956)
Pardon power Art 161; discretion Art 163; ordinance Art 213; report for President's Rule (Art 356)
TN Governor case (Apr 2025): 2-judge bench set timelines, 'deemed assent' to 10 Bills
Presidential Reference opinion (20 Nov 2025, 5 judges): no judicially fixed timelines, no 'deemed assent' — but no indefinite delay
traps: Governor can't PARDON a death sentence: that power is the President's (Art 72(1)(c)); Art 72(3) saves only the Governor's power to suspend/remit/commute; no court-martial power (Art 72(1)(a))
No impeachment; serves at President's pleasure — B.P. Singhal (2010): removal not arbitrary
Same Governor for 2+ States: emoluments shared as President decides (Art 158(3A)); no criminal proceedings during term (Art 361)

entities.name: President
entities.line: Art 52–62 | elected by elected MPs + elected MLAs (incl. Delhi & Puducherry) | 5 yrs | impeachment Art 61 | pardon Art 72
facts: Qualification: citizen, 35 yrs, qualified for LS
Election disputes → SC (Art 71)
Impeachment (Art 61): only for 'violation of the Constitution'; ¼ members sign, 14 days' notice, ⅔ of total membership
Veto: absolute, suspensive, pocket; must assent to Constitutional Amendment Bills (24th CAA 1971)
traps: Nominated MPs: vote in IMPEACHMENT but not in ELECTION
State MLCs & nominated MLAs not in electoral college
Money Bill can't be returned for reconsideration
Pardon (Art 72) covers court-martial + death sentence
Delhi & Puducherry MLAs added to electoral college by 70th CAA 1992; MLAs vote in the ELECTION but have NO role in IMPEACHMENT

entities.name: Vice-President
entities.line: Art 63–71 | elected by all MPs (elected + nominated) | 5 yrs | ex-officio RS Chairman (Art 64)
facts: Qualification: citizen, 35 yrs, qualified for RS
Electoral college: MPs only (no MLAs)
Removal (Art 67(b)): RS resolution by effective majority + LS agreement; 14 days' notice
Disputes → SC
traps: No 'impeachment' for VP — removal resolution starts only in Rajya Sabha
While acting as President, does not chair RS and gets President's salary
VP elected in a mid-term vacancy gets a FULL 5-yr term, not the remainder (Art 68(2)); resigns to President

entities.name: Lok Sabha Speaker
entities.line: Art 93 | elected by LS | removed by effective majority, 14 days' notice (Art 94) | decides Money Bill — final (Art 110(3)), certifies it (Art 110(4)) | decides defection (10th Sch)
facts: Vacates office just before first sitting of new LS
Speaker pro tem appointed by President
Casting vote only on a tie (Art 100)
Presides over joint sitting (Art 118(4))
Resigns to Deputy Speaker
traps: During own removal resolution: can't preside but CAN speak & vote in first instance (Art 96)
Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker
Art 93: LS 'shall' choose a Deputy Speaker, but no time limit is fixed

entities.name: Ordinance
entities.line: Art 123 (President) / Art 213 (Governor) | lapses 6 weeks after Parliament reassembles | re-promulgation fraud on Constitution — DC Wadhwa (1986), Krishna Kumar Singh (2017)
facts: Any time EXCEPT when BOTH Houses are in session (recess of one House is enough) + President satisfied immediate action needed (Art 123(1))
Can be retrospective; can't amend the Constitution
Max life: 6 months + 6 weeks
38th CAA made satisfaction final; 44th CAA undid it
traps: President/Governor can withdraw it any time
Governor needs President's instructions for an ordinance on a Bill that would need prior presidential sanction or be reserved (Art 213(1) proviso)

entities.name: Money Bill
entities.line: Art 110 | introduced only in LS, on President's recommendation (Art 117) | RS may delay max 14 days | Speaker's certificate final
facts: Contents in Art 110 (taxes, borrowing, Consolidated Fund…)
RS can only recommend within 14 days; LS may reject recommendations
Puttaswamy-Aadhaar (2018): Aadhaar Act upheld as Money Bill; Rojer Mathew (2019): referred to larger bench
traps: Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, not vice-versa
No joint sitting on a Money Bill
President can't return it (only assent or withhold)
NOT a Money Bill merely because it imposes fines/penalties, fees for licences/services, or local-body taxes (Art 110(2))

entities.name: President's Rule
entities.line: Art 356 | Parliament approval within 2 months | max 3 yrs (beyond 1 yr only with conditions — 44th CAA) | SR Bommai (1994): floor test, judicial review
facts: Ground: failure of constitutional machinery; Art 365 = non-compliance with Union directions
First use: Punjab 1951
State legislature suspended/dissolved; Parliament legislates for the State
Extension every 6 months; beyond 1 yr only if National Emergency + ECI certifies
traps: Approval by SIMPLE majority (Art 352 needs SPECIAL majority)
Dissolution of assembly reviewable — S.R. Bommai (1994)
Can be imposed on Governor's report 'or otherwise' (Art 356(1)); Bommai: Assembly only suspended until Parliament approves

entities.name: National Emergency
entities.line: Art 352 | approval within 1 month by special majority | 'armed rebellion' replaced 'internal disturbance' (44th CAA 1978) | imposed 1962, 1971, 1975
facts: Grounds: war, external aggression, armed rebellion
Only on written advice of Cabinet (44th CAA)
Art 358: Art 19 suspended automatically (war/external aggression only)
Art 359: other FRs suspended by Presidential order
LS can revoke by simple majority (special sitting on notice by 1/10 members)
traps: Art 20 & 21 can never be suspended (44th CAA)
Armed rebellion does NOT auto-suspend Art 19
Can cover the whole of India or ANY PART (42nd CAA 1976); can be proclaimed before actual war/aggression if danger is imminent

entities.name: Anti-defection (10th Schedule)
entities.line: 52nd CAA 1985 | presiding officer decides | merger exception needs ⅔ of legislature party (91st CAA 2003 removed ⅓ split) | Kihoto Hollohan (1992): decision open to judicial review
facts: Grounds: voluntarily giving up party membership; voting/abstaining against whip (unless condoned in 15 days)
Independent joining a party → disqualified; nominated member may join a party within 6 months
Keisham Meghachandra (2020): Speaker should decide within 3 months
traps: Speaker's decision 'final' (Para 6) but NOT immune — open to judicial review; Para 7 bar struck down (Kihoto Hollohan)
'Split' (⅓) exception deleted in 2003; only ⅔ merger survives
91st CAA 2003: disqualified defector barred from minister/remunerative political post till re-elected (Arts 75(1B), 164(1B), 361B); CoM capped at 15%

entities.name: Sixth Schedule
entities.line: Art 244(2) & 275(1) | tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram | Autonomous District Councils with legislative powers
facts: 10 Autonomous District Councils: Assam 3, Meghalaya 3, Tripura 1, Mizoram 3
District Council: max 30 members, ≤4 nominated by Governor, rest elected (BTC: up to 46); 5-yr term
Governor can create/reorganise autonomous districts
traps: Manipur is NOT under the 6th Schedule
Ladakh is not in the 6th Schedule (a recurring demand)

entities.name: Fifth Schedule
entities.line: Art 244(1) | Scheduled Areas in states other than the 4 NE (6th Sch) states | Tribes Advisory Council | PESA 1996 extends Panchayats
facts: Scheduled Areas declared by President
Governor sends annual report to President on Scheduled Areas
Tribes Advisory Council: up to 20 members, ¾ ST MLAs
10 States have Fifth Schedule areas
traps: Governor may direct that an Act of Parliament/State won't apply to a Scheduled Area
PESA 1996 applies to 5th Schedule areas, not 6th
TAC can be set up even in a State with STs but NO Scheduled Areas, if the President directs (5th Sch. para 4(1))

entities.name: Eighth Schedule
entities.line: Arts 344 & 351 | 22 languages | last added: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali (92nd CAA 2003)
facts: Originally 14 languages; Sindhi added 1967 (21st CAA)
Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali: 71st CAA 1992
Classical languages: 11 (Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali added Oct 2024)
traps: English is NOT in the 8th Schedule
Official language of the Union: Hindi in Devanagari (Art 343)
Pali & Prakrit = classical languages (2024) but NOT in the 8th Schedule; 96th CAA 2011 renamed Oriya → Odia

entities.name: Article 370
entities.line: Temporary provisions for J&K | made inoperative by Presidential Orders, Aug 2019 | J&K Reorganisation Act 2019 → UTs J&K and Ladakh | upheld by SC, Dec 2023
facts: Drafted by N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
Art 35A (via 1954 Presidential Order) also ended in 2019
In re Article 370 (11 Dec 2023, 5-judge bench): upheld; directed J&K polls by 30 Sep 2024
J&K Assembly elections held Sep–Oct 2024
traps: Art 370 text not deleted — made inoperative
Ladakh = UT without legislature; J&K = UT with legislature
SC (2023) did NOT rule on the validity of turning J&K State into a UT (relied on statehood assurance); upheld carving out UT Ladakh (Art 3)

entities.name: Panchayati Raj / ULBs
entities.line: 73rd CAA 1992: Part IX, 11th Sch, 29 subjects | 74th CAA 1992: Part IXA, 12th Sch, 18 subjects | in force 1993 | ≥⅓ seats & chairpersons reserved for women
facts: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957): 3-tier PRI; first at Nagaur, Rajasthan (2 Oct 1959)
Gram Sabha Art 243A; State Finance Commission Art 243I; State Election Commission Art 243K
Min. age 21; 5-yr term; fresh polls within 6 months of dissolution
24 April = National Panchayati Raj Day
traps: Intermediate tier optional in States with population < 20 lakh
Part IX not applicable to Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram (and some other areas)
Basis in DPSP: Art 40
State Election Commissioner appointed by Governor but removable only like an HC judge (Art 243K(2)); courts barred in panchayat poll matters (Art 243O)

entities.name: Basic Structure
entities.line: Kesavananda Bharati (1973), 13-judge bench | limits Art 368 amending power | applied: Indira Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975), Minerva Mills (1980)
facts: Golaknath (1967): Parliament can't amend FRs → reversed by 24th CAA 1971
Kesavananda decided 7:6
42nd CAA's Art 368(4),(5) struck down — Minerva Mills (1980)
I.R. Coelho (2007): 9th Schedule laws after 24 Apr 1973 reviewable
Elements incl.: supremacy of Constitution, secularism, federalism, judicial review, free & fair elections
traps: 'Basic structure' is not defined anywhere in the Constitution
Kesavananda overruled Golaknath (Parliament CAN amend FRs) & upheld 24th CAA; Waman Rao (1981) fixed the 24 Apr 1973 cut-off for 9th Sch.

entities.name: Collegium system
entities.line: Second Judges case (1993) + Third Judges (1998 advisory) | NJAC (99th CAA 2014) struck down in 2015 (Fourth Judges case)
facts: SC appointments: CJI + 4 senior-most (Third Judges 1998); HC appointments: HC collegium (CJ + 2) proposes → SC collegium (CJI + 2) decides
Govt may return a name once; reiteration binds
First Judges case (S.P. Gupta, 1981) had given primacy to the executive
traps: The word 'collegium' does not occur in the Constitution
Fourth Judges (NJAC) case 2015 decided 4:1 (Chelameswar J. dissented)

entities.name: Uniform Civil Code
entities.line: Art 44 (DPSP) | Goa follows Portuguese Civil Code (1867) | Uttarakhand UCC Act 2024: first state after Independence
facts: Art 44: 'State shall endeavour to secure a UCC'
Shah Bano (1985), Sarla Mudgal (1995) urged UCC
Uttarakhand UCC in force 27 Jan 2025 — marriage, divorce, succession, live-in registration; STs exempted | Gujarat = 2nd State (Act 2026; assent 17 Sep 2026; STs exempted)
traps: DPSPs are non-justiciable (Art 37)
21st Law Commission (2018): UCC 'neither necessary nor desirable at this stage'
Uttarakhand = first State to bring its UCC into force (27 Jan 2025)

entities.name: CVC
entities.line: CVC Act 2003 (body set up 1964, Santhanam Committee) | CVC + ≤2 VCs appointed by President on panel PM + HM + LoP | 4 yrs/65 | removal by President; misbehaviour after SC inquiry
facts: Apex vigilance body; supervises CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases
Annual report to President
traps: Statutory (2003), not constitutional
Advisory — cannot register criminal cases itself
CVC-led panel (CVC + VCs + Home, DoPT & Revenue Secretaries) recommends the ED Director
CVC is the designated agency for whistleblower complaints (PIDPI Resolution 2004)

entities.name: CBI
entities.line: Set up 1963 (MHA resolution); powers from DSPE Act 1946 | Director chosen by panel PM + LoP + CJI | 2-yr minimum tenure, extendable to 5 yrs (2021) | under DoPT
facts: Motto: Industry, Impartiality, Integrity
Needs State consent (Sec 6, DSPE Act) — several States withdrew general consent
India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL
Vineet Narain (1997): fixed 2-yr tenure for Director
traps: Not statutory — set up by executive resolution
Under DoPT (Ministry of Personnel), NOT the MHA
Santhanam Committee recommended both CVC (1964) and CBI (1963)
Director: extension 1 yr at a time, up to 5 yrs total (DSPE Amendment 2021)

entities.name: Lokpal
entities.line: Lokpal & Lokayuktas Act 2013 | Chair + up to 8 members (half judicial) | appointed by President on panel PM + Speaker + LoP + CJI + eminent jurist | 5 yrs/70
facts: First Lokpal: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose (2019)
PM covered — with exclusions (international relations, security, public order, atomic energy, space); inquiry needs ⅔ of full bench, in camera
States had to set up Lokayuktas within 1 year
First Lokayukta: Maharashtra (1971); idea from ARC (1966, Morarji Desai)
traps: Lokpal is statutory, not constitutional
Chair need not be a judge (ex-CJI/SC judge OR eminent person); ≥50% members from SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women
Term 'Lokpal' coined by L.M. Singhvi (1963)

entities.name: NHRC
entities.line: Protection of Human Rights Act 1993 | Chair: retired CJI or SC judge (2019 amendment) | appointed by President on panel PM + Speaker + HM + LoPs + RS Dy Chairman | 3 yrs/70
facts: Set up 12 Oct 1993; follows UN Paris Principles
Complaints within 1 yr of the incident
Ex-officio: chairpersons of NCSC, NCST, NCW, NCM, NCBC, NCPCR + Chief Commissioner for PwD
traps: Recommendations not binding; no power to punish
Chair & members eligible for re-appointment (2019 amendment); earlier the Chair was barred
Armed forces: can only seek a report from the Centre
SHRC chair/members appointed by Governor but removable only by the President

entities.name: NGT
entities.line: NGT Act 2010 | principal bench New Delhi + zonal benches Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai | disposal target 6 months | appeal to SC within 90 days
facts: Specialised court for environmental cases; follows natural justice, not CPC
Based on Art 21 (right to healthy environment)
traps: NGT does not hear Wildlife Protection Act 1972 cases (not in its Schedule I)
NGT Schedule I excludes Wildlife Protection Act 1972, Indian Forest Act 1927 & Forest Rights Act 2006
NGT can act suo motu (SC, MCGM v Ankita Sinha, 2021)

entities.name: NDMA
entities.line: Disaster Management Act 2005 | Chair: PM | lays down national DM policy & guidelines | NDRF raised 2006 under the Act
facts: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) under NDMA framework; NIDM for training
State: SDMA chaired by CM; District: DDMA chaired by Collector
traps: Sendai Framework 2015–2030 (7 targets, 4 priorities) replaced Hyogo Framework 2005–15
National Executive Committee chaired by the Union Home Secretary, not the PM

entities.name: Central Information Commission
entities.line: RTI Act 2005 (2019 amendment: tenure/salary set by Centre) | CIC + ≤10 ICs appointed by President on panel PM + LoP (LS) + Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM
facts: RTI Act 2005: reply in 30 days; 48 hrs if life/liberty involved
Exemptions: Sec 8; security/intelligence orgs: Sec 24 (except corruption/human-rights info)
traps: Tenure & salary now set by Centre (2019 amendment) — no longer fixed in the Act
CIC can penalise a PIO ₹250/day, max ₹25,000 (Sec 20); second appeal to CIC within 90 days (Sec 19(3))
DPDP Act 2023 (Sec 44(3)) amended RTI Sec 8(1)(j) — personal-information exemption widened

entities.name: TRAI
entities.line: TRAI Act 1997 | telecom & broadcasting regulator | disputes → TDSAT (2000)
traps: TDSAT also hears appeals under the IT Act 2000 & AERA Act 2008 (Finance Act 2017)
Telecommunications Act 2023 repealed the Indian Telegraph Act 1885

entities.name: CCI
entities.line: Competition Act 2002 (replaced MRTP Act 1969) | anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominance, combinations | appeals → NCLAT
traps: Under Ministry of Corporate Affairs; appeals: COMPAT till 2017, now NCLAT → SC
Competition (Amendment) Act 2023: deal-value threshold ₹2,000 cr; merger review cut 210 → 150 days

entities.name: SEBI
entities.line: Set up 1988; statutory under SEBI Act 1992 | HQ Mumbai | Chair + members appointed by Centre | securities market regulator
facts: Members: Chair + 2 Union officials (Finance & Corporate Affairs) + 1 RBI + 5 others (≥3 whole-time)
Quasi-legislative, executive & quasi-judicial powers
Appeals → Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) → SC
Commodity derivatives under SEBI since FMC merger (2015)
traps: Insurance → IRDAI; pensions → PFRDA (not SEBI)

entities.name: RBI
entities.line: RBI Act 1934; est. 1 Apr 1935 (Hilton Young Commission) | nationalised 1949 | HQ Mumbai | MPC (Sec 45ZB): 6 members; Governor has casting vote (Sec 45ZI) | inflation target 4% ±2%, retained till Mar 2031
facts: Hilton Young Commission 1926; HQ Calcutta → Mumbai (1937)
Nationalised 1 Jan 1949; first Indian Governor: C.D. Deshmukh
MPC: 3 RBI + 3 Govt nominees (4 yrs), quorum 4, ≥4 meetings/yr
Target set by GoI with RBI every 5 yrs; failure = CPI outside band for 3 straight quarters
Corridor: SDF (floor, since Apr 2022) < repo < MSF = bank rate (ceiling)
traps: CRR: kept with RBI, earns no interest; SLR: kept by banks themselves in liquid assets
SDF (no collateral) replaced reverse repo as the floor
Inflation index used for targeting = CPI (combined), not WPI
MPC external members: 4-yr term, NOT eligible for re-appointment

entities.name: FSSAI
entities.line: Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 | under MoHFW | sets science-based food standards
traps: FSS Act 2006 but FSSAI set up 2008; State Food Safety Index released on World Food Safety Day (7 June)

entities.name: NABARD
entities.line: Est. 12 Jul 1982 (NABARD Act 1981; Sivaraman Committee) | apex bank for agri & rural development | HQ Mumbai
facts: Refinances rural credit; RIDF for rural infrastructure
Supervises RRBs, StCBs & DCCBs (urban co-op banks under RBI)
traps: NABARD does not lend directly to individual farmers (refinances via banks)
Wholly owned by GoI; set up on CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman) recommendation

entities.name: NITI Aayog
entities.line: 2015, replaced Planning Commission | Chair: PM | Governing Council: CMs of States & UTs with legislature + LGs of other UTs | executive body (Cabinet resolution); policy think tank + cooperative federalism
facts: Formed 1 Jan 2015; first Governing Council meeting 8 Feb 2015
Vice-Chairperson & CEO appointed by PM; up to 4 Union ministers ex-officio
Publishes SDG India Index, Export Preparedness Index, Fiscal Health Index
DMEO (evaluation office) attached
traps: No power to allocate funds to States (unlike Planning Commission, set up 15 Mar 1950)
Neither constitutional nor statutory

entities.name: ISRO
entities.line: Est. 15 Aug 1969 | under Dept of Space (1972) | HQ Bengaluru | founder: Vikram Sarabhai
facts: Launchers: PSLV (polar/SSO), GSLV (GTO, cryogenic), LVM3 (heavy), SSLV (small)
Chandrayaan-3 landed near lunar south pole 23 Aug 2023 (= National Space Day)
Aditya-L1 in halo orbit at L1 (Jan 2024)
SpaDeX docking (Jan 2025) — India 4th nation to dock in space
Bharatiya Antariksh Station targeted by 2035
traps: L1 = Sun–Earth Lagrange point, ~1.5 mn km from Earth (not Earth–Moon)
Precursor INCOSPAR (1962, under DAE); Dept of Space created 1972
NSIL (2019) = commercial arm; IN-SPACe (2020) = authoriser of private players — neither is ISRO

entities.name: DRDO
entities.line: Est. 1958 | under MoD (Dept of Defence R&D) | HQ New Delhi
facts: IGMDP 1983 (Kalam): Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash, Nag
BrahMos: supersonic cruise missile, India–Russia JV
Nirbhay: subsonic cruise; Astra: BVR air-to-air; Akash: surface-to-air
traps: Agni & Prithvi are ballistic; BrahMos & Nirbhay are cruise missiles
Mission Divyastra (11 Mar 2024): Agni-5 with MIRV

entities.name: ICMR
entities.line: Est. 1911 as Indian Research Fund Association; renamed 1949 | under Dept of Health Research, MoHFW
facts: Apex body for biomedical research; HQ New Delhi
traps: Under Dept of Health Research (MoHFW), not DST/CSIR

entities.name: IMD
entities.line: Est. 1875 | under Ministry of Earth Sciences | HQ New Delhi | nodal agency for weather & cyclone warnings
facts: Issues cyclone names for the North Indian Ocean (WMO/ESCAP panel, 13 countries)
Monsoon onset over Kerala: normal date 1 June
traps: El Niño (warm east Pacific) usually weakens Indian monsoon; positive IOD usually strengthens it
Under MoES (not DST); Mission Mausam approved Sep 2024; IMD turned 150 on 15 Jan 2025

entities.name: NSO (MoSPI)
entities.line: National Statistics Office — 2019 merger of CSO + NSSO under MoSPI | releases GDP, CPI, IIP, PLFS
facts: New base years: GDP 2022-23 (Feb 2026), CPI 2024 (Feb 2026), IIP 2022-23 (2026)
WPI base revised to 2022-23; WPI is compiled by Office of Economic Adviser (DPIIT), not NSO
traps: CPI = retail, includes services; WPI = wholesale goods, no services
National Statistical Commission (2005, Rangarajan Commission rec.) is non-statutory

entities.name: Zonal Councils
entities.line: States Reorganisation Act 1956 | 5 zonal councils | Chair: Union Home Minister | advisory, statutory
facts: 5 councils: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern
Vice-chair rotates among member CMs
traps: North Eastern Council is separate (NEC Act 1971), not a zonal council
Zonal Councils statutory (SRA 1956) vs Inter-State Council constitutional (Art 263, set up 1990)
NEC: Union Home Minister ex-officio Chair (since 2018); Sikkim added 2002

entities.name: United Nations
entities.line: UN | 1945 (Charter, San Francisco) | HQ New York | 193 members | India founding member | peace, security, development
facts: Charter signed 26 Jun 1945; in force 24 Oct 1945 (UN Day)
6 principal organs: GA, SC, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ, Secretariat
Secretary-General: appointed by GA on SC recommendation, 5-yr term
traps: Trusteeship Council suspended since 1994 (Palau)
ICJ = only principal organ not in New York
GA resolutions are recommendatory; SC Chapter VII resolutions binding

entities.name: UN Security Council
entities.line: UNSC | 1945 | New York | 15 members: P5 (US, UK, France, Russia, China) + 10 elected for 2 yrs | India non-permanent 8 times (last 2021–22); seeks permanent seat
facts: Non-permanent members elected by GA (⅔), 5 each year; no immediate re-election
Presidency rotates monthly (alphabetical)
G4 (India, Brazil, Germany, Japan) seek permanent seats; 'Uniting for Consensus' opposes
traps: Word 'veto' is not in the Charter ('concurring votes')
P5 abstention ≠ veto

entities.name: World Trade Organization
entities.line: WTO | 1995 (succeeded GATT 1947; Marrakesh Agreement) | Geneva | 166 members | India founding member | rules-based trade; Ministerial Conference = top body | report: World Trade Report
facts: Uruguay Round 1986–94; Agreements: AoA, TRIPS, TRIMS, GATS, SPS
Ministerial Conference every 2 yrs: MC13 Abu Dhabi (2024), MC14 Yaoundé (2026)
Peace Clause (Bali 2013) protects public food stockholding
De minimis: 10% of production value (developing), 5% (developed)
traps: Appellate Body non-functional since Dec 2019
Amber box = trade-distorting (capped); Green box = minimal distortion (no cap)
Decisions by consensus

entities.name: International Monetary Fund
entities.line: IMF | 1944 Bretton Woods (in force Dec 1945; operations from Mar 1947) | Washington DC | 191 members | India founding member | BoP stability, SDRs | reports: World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report, Fiscal Monitor
facts: Quota decides votes & access
SDR basket: USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP (CNY since 2016)
India's ED also represents Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Bhutan
traps: IMF = balance-of-payments support; World Bank = development finance
SDR is a reserve asset, not a currency

entities.name: World Bank
entities.line: World Bank (IBRD 1944 + IDA 1960) | Washington DC | 189 members (IBRD) | India founding member | end extreme poverty | reports: World Development Report, Global Economic Prospects, B-READY (replaced Doing Business)
facts: World Bank Group: IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID
IDA = concessional loans to poorest countries
traps: India is NOT a member of ICSID
'World Bank' = only IBRD + IDA

entities.name: World Health Organization
entities.line: WHO | 1948 (7 Apr = World Health Day) | Geneva | India member; US (Jan 2026) & Argentina (2026) withdrew | health for all | report: World Health Statistics; Pandemic Agreement adopted 2025
facts: World Health Assembly (May, Geneva) is the decision body
SEARO (South-East Asia Regional Office) in New Delhi
Global Centre for Traditional Medicine: Jamnagar (2022)
IHR (2005) amended 2024
traps: Pakistan & Afghanistan are in WHO's EMRO (Cairo), not SEARO (New Delhi)

entities.name: UNESCO
entities.line: UN Educational, Scientific & Cultural Org | 1945 | Paris | India member | World Heritage (1972 Convention), Intangible Cultural Heritage lists | report: Global Education Monitoring Report

entities.name: UNEP
entities.line: UN Environment Programme | 1972 (Stockholm Conference) | Nairobi | global environmental authority | reports: Emissions Gap Report, Global Environment Outlook
facts: Hosts secretariats of CBD, CITES, Montreal Protocol (Ozone), Basel/Rotterdam/Stockholm
traps: UNFCCC secretariat is NOT under UNEP (Bonn, separate)

entities.name: UNFCCC
entities.line: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change | adopted 1992 (New York), signed at Rio Earth Summit 1992, in force 1994 | secretariat Bonn | India: non-Annex I party | COPs; Kyoto 1997, Paris 2015
facts: COP1 Berlin 1995; Kyoto Protocol 1997 (in force 2005)
Principle: CBDR-RC
Paris 2015: well below 2°C, pursue 1.5°C; NDCs every 5 yrs; Art 6 = carbon markets
COP28 Dubai: Loss & Damage Fund operational; COP29 Baku: NCQG $300 bn/yr by 2035; COP30 Belém (2025); COP31 Antalya, Türkiye (2026, Australia leads negotiations)
India: net zero 2070; 45% emission-intensity cut by 2030 (vs 2005); 50% non-fossil capacity target met in 2025
traps: India is non-Annex I — Kyoto targets applied only to Annex I
NDCs are nationally determined, not legally binding targets

entities.name: IPCC
entities.line: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change | 1988 by WMO + UNEP | Geneva | 195 members | assessment reports (AR6 2023; AR7 cycle underway)
facts: Working Groups: I physical science, II impacts & adaptation, III mitigation
AR6 Synthesis Report 2023
Nobel Peace Prize 2007 (with Al Gore)
traps: IPCC does no original research — assesses published literature
Set up by WMO + UNEP (1988); secretariat in Geneva hosted by WMO

entities.name: ILO
entities.line: International Labour Organization | 1919 (Treaty of Versailles) | Geneva | 187 members; tripartite (govts, employers, workers) | India founding member | report: World Employment and Social Outlook
traps: Only tripartite UN agency (governments, employers, workers)

entities.name: FAO
entities.line: Food and Agriculture Organization | 1945 | Rome | 195 members (incl. EU) | India member | report: State of Food Security and Nutrition (SOFI), State of the World's Forests
traps: SOFI report is joint: FAO + IFAD + UNICEF + WFP + WHO (not FAO alone)

entities.name: UNICEF
entities.line: UN Children's Fund | 1946 | New York | report: State of the World's Children
traps: Nobel Peace Prize 1965

entities.name: UN Human Rights Council
entities.line: UNHRC | 2006 (replaced UN Commission on Human Rights) | Geneva | 47 members elected for 3 yrs | Universal Periodic Review
facts: Seats by regional groups; max 2 consecutive terms
traps: Members elected by the UN General Assembly (secret ballot), not by the UNSC

entities.name: International Court of Justice
entities.line: ICJ | 1945 (UN principal judicial organ) | The Hague (Peace Palace) | 15 judges, 9-yr terms | advisory + contentious jurisdiction
facts: Judges elected by GA + SC (absolute majority in both)
traps: ICJ settles disputes between STATES; ICC tries INDIVIDUALS

entities.name: International Criminal Court
entities.line: ICC | Rome Statute 1998, in force 2002 | The Hague | India NOT a party | genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, aggression
facts: Tries individuals; complements national courts (complementarity)
traps: Not a UN organ (independent treaty body); India, USA, China not parties

entities.name: IAEA
entities.line: International Atomic Energy Agency | 1957 | Vienna | India founding member | 'Atoms for Peace'; safeguards
traps: Not a UN specialised agency — autonomous, reports to UNGA & UNSC; Nobel Peace Prize 2005

entities.name: NATO
entities.line: North Atlantic Treaty Organization | 1949 (Washington Treaty) | Brussels | 32 members (Finland 2023, Sweden 2024) | Art 5 collective defence
facts: Art 5 invoked only once — after 9/11 (2001)
traps: Treaty signed in Washington (1949) but HQ Brussels; 12 founders → 32

entities.name: G20
entities.line: Group of 20 | 1999 (leaders' summits from 2008) | no secretariat; rotating presidency | 19 countries + EU + African Union (joined 2023, India's presidency) | India member
facts: Born after Asian Financial Crisis (1997–98)
~85% world GDP, ~75% trade, ~⅔ population
India 2023 presidency: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — One Earth, One Family, One Future'; New Delhi Declaration
2025: South Africa; 2026: USA
traps: No permanent secretariat (troika system)
Spain is a permanent guest, not a member

entities.name: G7
entities.line: Group of Seven | 1975 | no secretariat | US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada (+EU) | India NOT member; invited as outreach partner
facts: Was G8 with Russia (1997–2014)
traps: 1975 Rambouillet = G6; Canada joined 1976 → G7

entities.name: BRICS
entities.line: BRICS | 2009 first summit (Yekaterinburg); South Africa joined 2010 | expanded 2024 (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE) + Indonesia 2025 | 11 members as listed by BRICS (incl. Saudi Arabia, which has not formally confirmed) + 10 partner countries | India founding member; India chairs 2026 (18th summit) | NDB, Shanghai
facts: 'BRIC' coined 2001 (Jim O'Neill); Contingent Reserve Arrangement $100 bn
17th summit: Rio de Janeiro (2025)
traps: NDB HQ Shanghai; first NDB President: K.V. Kamath (India)

entities.name: SCO
entities.line: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation | 2001 | secretariat Beijing; RATS Tashkent | 10 members (Iran 2023, Belarus 2024) | India full member 2017
facts: Grew from 'Shanghai Five' (1996)
Official languages: Russian & Chinese
India & Pakistan full members 2017 (Astana)
2025 summit: Tianjin
traps: Secretariat Beijing; RATS (anti-terror) in Tashkent
Mongolia & Afghanistan are observers, not members | Tianjin 2025: single 'SCO Partner' status to replace observer/dialogue partner

entities.name: Quad
entities.line: Quadrilateral Security Dialogue | 2007, revived 2017 | India, US, Japan, Australia | free & open Indo-Pacific
facts: Origin: 2004 tsunami core group
Leaders' summits since 2021
Initiatives: IPMDA (maritime awareness), Quad Fellowship
traps: Not a military alliance; no secretariat or treaty

entities.name: ASEAN
entities.line: Association of Southeast Asian Nations | 1967 (Bangkok Declaration) | Jakarta | 11 members (Timor-Leste admitted 2025) | India: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership 2022; Act East
facts: Founders: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand
India: sectoral partner 1992 → dialogue partner 1995 → summit 2002
ASEAN–India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) 2009
India in East Asia Summit (2005) & ASEAN Regional Forum
traps: India is NOT in RCEP (opted out 2019)

entities.name: SAARC
entities.line: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation | 1985 (Dhaka) | Kathmandu | 8 members (Afghanistan 2007) | largely dormant since 2016
traps: 9 observers incl. China, USA, EU, Myanmar — China is NOT a member; last summit: 18th, Kathmandu 2014

entities.name: BIMSTEC
entities.line: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical & Economic Cooperation | 1997 (Bangkok Declaration) | Dhaka | 7 members (5 South Asia + Myanmar, Thailand) | Charter in force 2024
facts: Members: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand
6th summit Bangkok (Apr 2025): Bangkok Vision 2030
traps: Pakistan, Maldives, Afghanistan are not members
Began 1997 as BIST-EC (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand); Myanmar joined 1997; Nepal & Bhutan 2004

entities.name: IORA
entities.line: Indian Ocean Rim Association | 1997 | Ebene, Mauritius | 23 members | India founding member
traps: France is a member (2020); US & China are only dialogue partners

entities.name: European Union
entities.line: EU | 1993 (Maastricht Treaty) | Brussels | 27 members | India–EU Strategic Partnership since 2004
facts: Euro area: 21 of 27 members (Bulgaria joined 1 Jan 2026)

entities.name: AIIB
entities.line: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank | 2016 | Beijing | India founding member and 2nd-largest shareholder
facts: Proposed by China (2013)
traps: China = largest shareholder; India 2nd largest

entities.name: New Development Bank
entities.line: NDB (BRICS bank) | agreed 2014 (Fortaleza), operational 2015 | Shanghai | equal founding shares of BRICS-5
facts: Authorised capital $100 bn
traps: First President K.V. Kamath (India)

entities.name: Asian Development Bank
entities.line: ADB | 1966 | Manila | 69 members | India founding member | report: Asian Development Outlook
facts: President traditionally Japanese
traps: HQ Manila ≠ AIIB Beijing; 69 members (50 regional + 19 non-regional)

entities.name: OPEC
entities.line: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries | 1960 (Baghdad) | Vienna | 11 members (UAE exited May 2026; Angola 2024) | OPEC+ adds Russia etc.
facts: Founders (Baghdad 1960): Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela
Exits: Qatar 2019, Ecuador 2020, Angola 2024, UAE 2026
traps: HQ Vienna (Austria) — not in West Asia

entities.name: IEA
entities.line: International Energy Agency | 1974 (after 1973 oil shock) | Paris | only OECD countries eligible for membership | India: association country (2017) | report: World Energy Outlook
facts: Members must hold oil stocks = 90 days of net imports
Flagship: World Energy Outlook
traps: India is NOT a full member (association country)
India AND China are association countries, not members

entities.name: International Solar Alliance
entities.line: ISA | launched 2015 at COP21 Paris by India & France | HQ Gurugram | first treaty-based intl body HQ'd in India
facts: Framework Agreement in force 6 Dec 2017
'One Sun One World One Grid' (OSOWOG)
Membership open to all UN member states (amended Framework Agreement)
traps: HQ: Gurugram (Haryana) — not Delhi

entities.name: FATF

concepts.name: Joint sitting
concepts.line: Art 108 | called by President | presided by Speaker | deadlock on ordinary (and financial) bills
facts: Held 3 times: 1961 Dowry Prohibition, 1978 Banking Service Commission (Repeal), 2002 POTA
traps: No joint sitting for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills

concepts.name: Quorum of a House
concepts.line: 1/10 of the total members of the House (Art 100(3))

concepts.name: Zero Hour
concepts.line: LS: right after Question Hour (12 noon) | RS: 11 am, before Question Hour (since 2014) | Indian innovation (1962)
traps: Zero Hour is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure

concepts.name: Money Bill
concepts.line: Art 110 | only in Lok Sabha, on President's recommendation | Speaker's certificate is final | RS: recommend within 14 days
traps: RS can only recommend; LS may reject its recommendations
No joint sitting on a Money Bill

concepts.name: Right to Education
concepts.line: Art 21A (6–14 yrs) | added by 86th CAA 2002 | RTE Act 2009 (in force 1 Apr 2010)
facts: 86th CAA also added Art 51A(k) duty (parents) and changed Art 45 (early childhood care)

concepts.name: Right to Property
concepts.line: Removed from Fundamental Rights by 44th CAA 1978 | now a constitutional/legal right under Art 300A
traps: Art 300A is in Part XII, not Part III

concepts.name: Article 32
concepts.line: Right to constitutional remedies | SC issues 5 writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto
facts: Ambedkar called Art 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution
traps: HC writ power (Art 226) is wider — also for legal rights

concepts.name: NOTA
concepts.line: 'None of the Above' on EVMs since 2013 (SC, PUCL v Union of India)
traps: Even if NOTA gets most votes, the candidate with the most votes wins

concepts.name: Model Code of Conduct
concepts.line: Issued by ECI; in force from announcement of schedule till results | evolved by consensus of parties
traps: MCC has no statutory backing (not a law)

concepts.name: Representation of the People Acts
concepts.line: RPA 1950: electoral rolls, seat allocation, delimitation-related | RPA 1951: conduct of elections, disqualifications, corrupt practices
traps: Disqualification for corrupt practices is under RPA 1951, not 1950

concepts.name: Consumer Price Index
concepts.line: Compiled by NSO (MoSPI) | new series base 2024 | RBI's inflation target is CPI (combined): 4% ±2%
facts: Core inflation = headline minus food & fuel
traps: CPI includes services; WPI does not

concepts.name: Wholesale Price Index
concepts.line: Compiled by Office of Economic Adviser (DPIIT, MoCI) | goods only, no services
traps: Disinflation = falling rate of inflation; deflation = negative inflation

concepts.name: GDP deflator
concepts.line: Nominal GDP ÷ real GDP × 100 | broadest price measure (all goods & services produced)

concepts.name: Repo rate & LAF corridor
concepts.line: Repo: RBI lends to banks overnight against G-secs | SDF (no collateral) = floor | MSF = ceiling
facts: Repo set by the 6-member Monetary Policy Committee (RBI Act Sec 45ZB)
traps: Higher repo → costlier credit (contractionary)

concepts.name: CRR & SLR
concepts.line: CRR: % of NDTL kept as cash with RBI (no interest) | SLR: % of NDTL held by banks in liquid assets (cash, gold, G-secs)
traps: CRR is held with RBI; SLR is held by the bank itself

concepts.name: Open market operations
concepts.line: RBI buys/sells G-secs to manage liquidity
traps: OMO purchase injects liquidity; OMO sale absorbs it

concepts.name: Deposit insurance
concepts.line: DICGC (RBI subsidiary) | covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal + interest)
traps: Limit is per bank, not per account

concepts.name: Payments banks
concepts.line: Accept deposits (up to ₹2 lakh per customer), remittances | cannot lend or issue credit cards
traps: Payments banks cannot give loans

concepts.name: Fiscal deficit
concepts.line: Total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts) | primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments
facts: FRBM Act 2003 sets the fiscal-responsibility framework

concepts.name: Funds of the Union
concepts.line: Consolidated Fund: Art 266(1) | Public Account: Art 266(2) | Contingency Fund: Art 267
traps: Contingency Fund is at the disposal of the President (executive), not Parliament
Charged expenditure is not voted (only discussed)

concepts.name: Union Budget terms
concepts.line: Budget = Annual Financial Statement (Art 112) | Vote on Account (Art 116) | Appropriation Bill (Art 114)

concepts.name: Balance of payments
concepts.line: Current account + capital account (+ errors & omissions) | CAD = imports of goods & services exceed exports + net transfers
traps: Remittances are in the current account (secondary income)

concepts.name: FDI vs FPI
concepts.line: FDI: any stake in an unlisted co, or ≥ 10% in a listed co (FEMA NDI Rules 2019) | FPI: < 10% in a listed co

concepts.name: Forex reserves
concepts.line: Foreign currency assets + gold + SDRs + reserve tranche position in the IMF | managed by RBI

concepts.name: REER
concepts.line: Real effective exchange rate: trade-weighted rupee value adjusted for inflation
traps: REER rising = rupee's real appreciation (exports less competitive)

concepts.name: Eight core industries
concepts.line: Index by Office of Economic Adviser (DPIIT) | coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, electricity

concepts.name: Index of Industrial Production
concepts.line: Compiled by NSO (MoSPI) | measures volume of industrial output
traps: IIP measures volume, not prices

concepts.name: Minimum Support Price
concepts.line: Announced by CCEA on CACP's advice | CACP (1965) under MoA&FW | 22 mandated crops | set at ≥ 1.5× A2+FL cost since 2018-19
traps: MSP has no statutory backing
Sugarcane gets FRP (Fair & Remunerative Price), not MSP

concepts.name: National Park vs Sanctuary
concepts.line: Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 | National Park: no grazing/private rights | Sanctuary: some activities allowed
traps: A sanctuary can be upgraded to a national park, not the reverse

concepts.name: Tiger Reserve
concepts.line: Notified by the State on NTCA's advice (Sec 38V, WPA 1972) | core + buffer zones

concepts.name: Eco-sensitive zones
concepts.line: Notified under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986 around protected areas

concepts.name: Conservation & Community Reserves
concepts.line: Added by WPA amendment 2002 | Conservation: govt land | Community: private/community land

concepts.name: Biosphere reserves
concepts.line: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) programme | core, buffer, transition zones
traps: Biosphere reserves are not created under the Wildlife (Protection) Act

concepts.name: Kigali Amendment
concepts.line: 2016 amendment to the Montreal Protocol | phases down HFCs | India's freeze year 2028
traps: Kigali targets HFCs, not methane
Montreal Protocol = ozone layer; Kyoto = greenhouse gases

concepts.name: Global Methane Pledge
concepts.line: Launched at COP26 (2021) | cut methane 30% from 2020 levels by 2030
traps: India has not signed it

concepts.name: Net zero
concepts.line: India's net-zero target: 2070 (announced at COP26, Glasgow, 2021)

concepts.name: Air Quality Index
concepts.line: 8 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb | 6 categories (good → severe)
traps: Ground-level ozone is a pollutant; stratospheric ozone is protective

concepts.name: National Clean Air Programme
concepts.line: Launched 2019 by MoEFCC | city-level clean-air plans

concepts.name: GRAP
concepts.line: Graded Response Action Plan for Delhi-NCR | enforced by CAQM (Commission for Air Quality Management)

concepts.name: Single-use plastics
concepts.line: Ban on identified items from 1 Jul 2022 (Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules 2021)

concepts.name: India State of Forest Report
concepts.line: Biennial | by Forest Survey of India (Dehradun), MoEFCC

concepts.name: Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023
concepts.line: Renamed the 1980 Act as Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam

concepts.name: El Niño & La Niña
concepts.line: El Niño: warm central/east Pacific → usually weaker Indian monsoon | La Niña: cool → usually stronger monsoon | together: ENSO
traps: ENSO is a Pacific phenomenon; IOD is the Indian Ocean's own

concepts.name: Indian Ocean Dipole
concepts.line: Positive IOD: warmer west Indian Ocean → usually aids the Indian monsoon | can offset El Niño's drying effect

concepts.name: Tropical cyclones
concepts.line: N Indian Ocean names: WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones, 13 member countries | IMD New Delhi is the regional centre
traps: Cyclones rotate anticlockwise in the N Hemisphere, clockwise in the S Hemisphere

concepts.name: Sendai Framework
concepts.line: 2015–2030 framework for disaster risk reduction (UN)

concepts.name: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF)
concepts.line: Sudden release of water from a lake dammed by a glacier or moraine | triggers: avalanche/landslide into the lake, earthquake, heavy rain, dam erosion
facts: Oct 2023: South Lhonak lake (Sikkim) GLOF damaged the Teesta-III dam at Chungthang
NDMA has issued guidelines on GLOF management
traps: A GLOF needs no rainfall — a moraine/ice dam failure alone can trigger it

concepts.name: Cloudburst
concepts.line: IMD: rainfall ≥ 10 cm in an hour over ~20–30 sq km | mostly in hilly terrain (orographic lift)
traps: Defined by intensity (per hour), not by the day's total rainfall

concepts.name: Heatwave (IMD)
concepts.line: Max temp ≥ 40°C plains / ≥ 37°C coast / ≥ 30°C hills, and departure ≥ 4.5°C (severe ≥ 6.5°C) | or actual max ≥ 45°C (severe ≥ 47°C)

concepts.name: Western disturbance
concepts.line: Extra-tropical storms from the Mediterranean region carried by the subtropical westerly jet | winter rain/snow in NW India; helps rabi wheat

concepts.name: ISRO launch vehicles
concepts.line: PSLV → polar/sun-synchronous | GSLV → geosynchronous transfer (cryogenic upper stage) | LVM3 → heavy lift | SSLV → small satellites
traps: Geostationary orbit ≈ 35,786 km above the equator; LEO < 2,000 km

concepts.name: Indian missiles
concepts.line: Ballistic: Agni, Prithvi | Cruise: BrahMos (supersonic), Nirbhay (subsonic) | Akash: SAM | Astra: BVR air-to-air | Nag: anti-tank
traps: Hypersonic = above Mach 5; supersonic = Mach 1–5

concepts.name: National Quantum Mission
concepts.line: Approved 2023 | ₹6,003 crore | till 2030-31 | DST nodal

concepts.name: IndiaAI Mission
concepts.line: Approved Mar 2024 | ₹10,372 crore | MeitY

concepts.name: India Semiconductor Mission
concepts.line: Launched Dec 2021 | under Digital India Corporation (MeitY)

concepts.name: DPDP Act 2023
concepts.line: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 | Data Protection Board of India | Rules notified Nov 2025

concepts.name: Geographical Indication
concepts.line: GI of Goods (Registration & Protection) Act 1999, in force 2003 | registry: Chennai | first GI: Darjeeling Tea | valid 10 yrs, renewable
traps: GI is a collective right of producers, not an individual patent

concepts.name: World Heritage Convention
concepts.line: UNESCO, 1972 | India ratified 1977 | India: 45 sites (37 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed) as of 2026 | 46th WH Committee session hosted in New Delhi (Jul 2024)
traps: Khangchendzonga NP (Sikkim) is India's only Mixed site

concepts.name: Human Development Index
concepts.line: By UNDP (Human Development Report) | health, education, income

concepts.name: Global Hunger Index
concepts.line: By Welthungerhilfe & Concern Worldwide
traps: GHI is not by FAO or WFP

concepts.name: Global Gender Gap Report
concepts.line: By World Economic Forum

concepts.name: World Press Freedom Index
concepts.line: By Reporters Without Borders (RSF)

concepts.name: Global Innovation Index
concepts.line: By WIPO

concepts.name: World Happiness Report
concepts.line: By Oxford Wellbeing Research Centre, with Gallup & UN SDSN

concepts.name: SDG India Index
concepts.line: By NITI Aayog

concepts.name: Logistics Performance Index
concepts.line: By World Bank

concepts.name: Ajanta Caves
concepts.line: Maharashtra (Chh. Sambhajinagar district), Waghora river | Buddhist rock-cut caves, c. 2nd c BCE–6th c CE | WHS 1983
facts: Famous for murals (e.g. Padmapani)

concepts.name: Ellora Caves
concepts.line: Maharashtra | Buddhist, Hindu & Jain caves (c. 600–1000 CE) | WHS 1983
facts: Kailasa temple (Cave 16): monolithic, built under Rashtrakuta king Krishna I
traps: Ellora has caves of three faiths; Ajanta is only Buddhist

concepts.name: Agra Fort
concepts.line: Uttar Pradesh, on the Yamuna | Mughal red sandstone fort begun by Akbar (1565) | WHS 1983

concepts.name: Taj Mahal
concepts.line: Agra, UP, on the Yamuna | built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal (17th c) | WHS 1983

concepts.name: Konark Sun Temple
concepts.line: Odisha | 13th c, Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I | Surya's chariot: 24 wheels, 7 horses | WHS 1984
facts: Called the 'Black Pagoda' by European sailors

concepts.name: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
concepts.line: Tamil Nadu (Coromandel coast) | Pallava, 7th–8th c | Shore Temple, Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance | WHS 1984

concepts.name: Churches and Convents of Goa
concepts.line: Old Goa | Portuguese colonial churches | Basilica of Bom Jesus holds St Francis Xavier's relics | WHS 1986

concepts.name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
concepts.line: Madhya Pradesh | Chandela dynasty, c. 950–1050 CE | Hindu & Jain temples, Nagara style | WHS 1986
facts: Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest temple

concepts.name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
concepts.line: Karnataka, on the Tungabhadra | last capital of the Vijayanagara Empire | WHS 1986
facts: Vittala temple's stone chariot

concepts.name: Fatehpur Sikri
concepts.line: Uttar Pradesh | Akbar's capital (built c. 1571–1585) | Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid | WHS 1986

concepts.name: Group of Monuments at Pattadakal
concepts.line: Karnataka, on the Malaprabha | Chalukyas of Badami, 7th–8th c | blend of Nagara & Dravida styles | WHS 1987
facts: Virupaksha temple built by Queen Lokamahadevi

concepts.name: Elephanta Caves
concepts.line: Gharapuri island, Mumbai harbour | rock-cut Shiva cave temples | Trimurti (Sadashiva) sculpture | WHS 1987

concepts.name: Great Living Chola Temples
concepts.line: Tamil Nadu | Brihadisvara (Thanjavur, Rajaraja I, completed 1010) + Gangaikondacholapuram (Rajendra I) + Airavatesvara (Darasuram, Rajaraja II) | WHS 1987, extended 2004

concepts.name: Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi
concepts.line: Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh | Great Stupa commissioned by Ashoka (3rd c BCE) | WHS 1989

concepts.name: Humayun's Tomb
concepts.line: Delhi | built by Humayun's widow Bega Begum (1560s–1570s) | first garden-tomb of the subcontinent | WHS 1993

concepts.name: Qutb Minar and its Monuments
concepts.line: Delhi | begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, completed by Iltutmish | Iron Pillar (Gupta era) in the complex | WHS 1993

concepts.name: Mountain Railways of India
concepts.line: Darjeeling Himalayan (1999) + Nilgiri (2005) + Kalka–Shimla (2008) | one serial WHS

concepts.name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex
concepts.line: Bodh Gaya, Bihar | site of the Buddha's enlightenment | WHS 2002

concepts.name: Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka
concepts.line: Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh | prehistoric rock paintings | WHS 2003

concepts.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
concepts.line: Mumbai | Victorian Gothic railway station by F. W. Stevens (1878–1888) | WHS 2004

concepts.name: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
concepts.line: Panchmahal district, Gujarat | pre-Mughal Islamic capital of Mahmud Begada | WHS 2004

concepts.name: Red Fort Complex
concepts.line: Delhi | built by Shah Jahan (1639–1648) as the palace of Shahjahanabad | WHS 2007

concepts.name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
concepts.line: Rajasthan | astronomical observatory of Sawai Jai Singh II (early 18th c) | Samrat Yantra: world's largest stone sundial | WHS 2010
traps: Only the Jaipur Jantar Mantar is a WHS, not Delhi's

concepts.name: Hill Forts of Rajasthan
concepts.line: 6 forts: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber, Jaisalmer | WHS 2013

concepts.name: Rani-ki-Vav
concepts.line: Patan, Gujarat | stepwell on the Saraswati | built by Queen Udayamati (Chaulukya/Solanki), 11th c | WHS 2014
facts: Pictured on the ₹100 note

concepts.name: Nalanda Mahavihara
concepts.line: Bihar | Buddhist monastic university, 5th c CE (Gupta era) to 13th c | WHS 2016

concepts.name: Architectural Work of Le Corbusier
concepts.line: Transnational serial site (7 countries) | India: Capitol Complex, Chandigarh | WHS 2016

concepts.name: Historic City of Ahmadabad
concepts.line: Gujarat | founded by Sultan Ahmad Shah I (1411), on the Sabarmati | WHS 2017
traps: India's first World Heritage City

concepts.name: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai
concepts.line: Mumbai, around the Oval Maidan | WHS 2018

concepts.name: Jaipur City
concepts.line: Rajasthan | planned walled city founded 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II | WHS 2019
traps: India's second World Heritage City (after Ahmadabad)

concepts.name: Ramappa Temple
concepts.line: Palampet, Mulugu district, Telangana | Kakatiya; built 1213 CE by Recharla Rudra, general of Ganapati Deva | WHS 2021 as 'Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple'
facts: Shikhara of light, porous 'floating' bricks; sandbox foundation
Presiding deity: Ramalingeswara (Shiva)
traps: Named after its chief sculptor Ramappa, not the deity

concepts.name: Dholavira
concepts.line: Khadir Bet, Kutch, Gujarat | Harappan city with advanced water management | WHS 2021
facts: India's first Harappan site on the WHS list

concepts.name: Santiniketan
concepts.line: Birbhum, West Bengal | founded by Rabindranath Tagore (Visva-Bharati) | WHS 2023

concepts.name: Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
concepts.line: Karnataka | Chennakeshava (Belur), Hoysaleswara (Halebidu), Keshava (Somanathapura) | WHS 2023

concepts.name: Moidams of Charaideo
concepts.line: Assam | mound-burials of the Ahom dynasty | WHS 2024
traps: First cultural WHS from the Northeast

concepts.name: Maratha Military Landscapes of India
concepts.line: 12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra + Gingee in Tamil Nadu | WHS 2025

concepts.name: Sarnath
concepts.line: Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh | site of the Buddha's first sermon | Dhamek Stupa; Ashokan Lion Capital found here | WHS 2026
facts: The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath is India's National Emblem
